device.name: Thorlabs Kinesis brushless DC motor controller channel

facts.text: The Kinesis wrapper loads the Thorlabs Kinesis .NET assemblies through pythonnet and appends 'C:\Program Files\Thorlabs\Kinesis' to sys.path
The module builds the device list at import and filters the connected serial numbers by device prefix
Kinesis.connect connects the device, waits up to 5000 ms for settings initialization and starts polling every 250 ms
Kinesis.close stops polling, disconnects and disposes the device
Kinesis.stop calls Stop(0) on the device
Kinesis.move_abs converts the position to System.Decimal and calls MoveTo with a callback (or 0); home calls Home with the same callback handling
is_homed, is_moving and is_homing read the IsHomed, IsInMotion and IsHoming flags of the device Status
get_target_position returns the device Position converted from System.Decimal to float
get_units returns the unit converter's RealUnits, or default_units when reading it fails
BrushlessDCMotor.connect accepts a serial number from the controller's device list and init_channel creates and connects a BrushlessMotorChannel
BrushlessDCMotor forwards get_position, move_abs, home, is_homed, stop, get_units and get_target_position to the channel selected by channel index
The PyMoDAQ BrushlessDCMotor plugin reads the position with get_position(axis) and the unit with get_units(axis)
The PyMoDAQ plugin maps the axis names '1', '2' and '3' to controller channel indices 1, 2 and 3
The PyMoDAQ plugin applies its user-configured bounds with check_bound before an absolute move; the bound is a PyMoDAQ setting, not a controller limit
The PyMoDAQ plugin implements a relative move by adding the offset to the current position and calling the controller's absolute move
The README describes the BrushlessDCMotor plugin as Kinesis control of a DC brushless motor tested with the BBD201 controller
The package declares pythonnet and pywin32 as dependencies
